Messages.Author: Ben Peal
Messages.Body:
Some questions...

1) When used for a strike, does a Bomb burn as the strike is declared
or during strike resolution?

2) Can multiple Ghoul Retainers "share" a Bomb during the same round
of combat? What happens?

3) If a Ghoul Retainer uses a Bomb for damage, does the Bomb burn at
the end of combat, even though it was not used for a strike by a
minion?

4) May ammo cards be played on a gun being used by a Ghoul Retainer?

5) If the answer to 4) is "yes", does the ammo card's effect apply to
damage inflicted by other Ghoul Retainers "sharing" the gun in the
same round?

6) May Temptation counters be burned to control a minion during combat?

- Ben Peal, Prince of Boston
fu...@mindstorm.com

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Ben Peal wrote:
>
> Some questions...
>
> 1) When used for a strike, does a Bomb burn as the strike is declared
> or during strike resolution?

When "used" - during strike reolution.

> 2) Can multiple Ghoul Retainers "share" a Bomb during the same round
> of combat? What happens?

Yes. It burns during strike resolution.

> 3) If a Ghoul Retainer uses a Bomb for damage, does the Bomb burn at
> the end of combat, even though it was not used for a strike by a
> minion?

Yes. The clarification of card text needs further clarifying, I guess.

> 4) May ammo cards be played on a gun being used by a Ghoul Retainer?

No.

> 5) If the answer to 4) is "yes", does the ammo card's effect apply to
> damage inflicted by other Ghoul Retainers "sharing" the gun in the
> same round?
>
> 6) May Temptation counters be burned to control a minion during combat?

Yes.

Messages.Body:
dave...@hotmail.com (hamdamcwa) wrote in message news:<9e10847c.0109...@posting.google.com>...

I still don't understand what Charisma has to do with all this. It
lowers the cost of an ally. Ghoul Retainer, last I checked, was a
retainer.

You could just go ahead and pay full price for them all and Heidelburg
them over, but GOOD LORD that's a lot of pool. Each additional
card+action+2 pool nets you an extra 5 damage, with each use of the
damage eating up at least 3 cards (Bomb + Flesh of Marble + get into
combat) and 1 pool.

Assuming you want to do 15 damage (what's the point in more?), it'll
cost you a one time cost of 8 pool (Heidelberg + 3 ghouls), 4 cards, 3
actions, and 1 master phase (ignoring the cost of the extra vampires
you'll need). Each time doing it will cost 2 actions (Bomb + rush), 3
cards, and 1 blood (assuming that Black Cat gets the Bomb and you
Heidelberg it over). If you use it on 5 vampires, assuming no dodges,
it costs 8 pool, 19 cards, 5 blood, 13 actions, and a master phase.

If you want to do 15 damage with superior Potence, it'll cost you 9
cards, 1 blood, and 1 action each time (rush, Torn Signpost, 5
Increased Strength, Undead Strength, and FoM or SoS or whatever to
prevent opponent's damage). To do it to 5 vampires costs 45 cards, 5
blood, and 5 actions.

It only gets worse if you use Lambach, or a Gangrel with Ritual
Challenge or Gangrel Revel. Is using fewer cards really worth that
many actions and pool? The only way to reduce pool cost is to take
all of the recruit actions with Regina (I believe), and she dosen't
have most of the other disciplines that would make things easier. You
can cut down on the number actions using obf or chi, but still... How
many times do you really *need* to do that much damage. Once you do
more than 2 above the vamp's capacity, they're either gonna prevent it
all or go to torpor. The efficiency of the Ghoul method only gets
worse with less Ghouls, and 15 damage seems to be the limit of
effective damage. You could do a million damage and it wouldn't be
any different from doing a hundred, which would be only marginally
different from doing 15.

Just in case you weren't aware of the special terminology I was using,
Lambach, as used in the above statement, actually means "Lasverinus".
This was not, of course, a mistake, but simply ignorance that many
people might not be aware of my special terminology. For future
reference, "Bear Paw" is sometimes translated as "Badger", and
"Emerson Bridges" or "that Toreador with PRE" are sometimes used in
place of "Gideon Fontaine", despite the fact that he is neither a
Toreador, nor the Prince of Washington (or of Madison County, for that
matter).
